quest.title: Speed Safari
quest.prompt: Find three animals that are faster than a car on the highway (over 100 km/h, 62 mph).
quest.rubric: Counts: an animal whose top speed stated on the page is over 100 km/h or 62 mph, for example cheetah, peregrine falcon, sailfish, pronghorn. Does not count: animals without a stated speed over 100 km/h, vehicles, fictional animals.

page.title: Cheetah - Wander Encyclopedia
page.text:
The cheetah is a large wild cat that lives mostly in Africa, with a small group in Iran.
It is the fastest land animal. A cheetah can sprint at about 110 km/h (68 mph) for short bursts, which is faster than a car on the highway.
Speed
Its long legs, light body and flexible spine let it cover about 7 meters in a single stride. The long tail works like a rudder when it turns.
A chase usually lasts less than a minute, because running that fast makes the cheetah very hot and tired.
Food
Cheetahs hunt during the day, mostly gazelles and impalas. They rely on their sharp eyesight rather than smell.
Family life
A mother cheetah raises her cubs alone for about 18 months. The cubs have fluffy grey fur on their backs that helps them hide in tall grass.
Today fewer than 7,000 adult cheetahs live in the wild, so many groups work to protect them.
